subject: physiotherapy
intro: Physiotherapy leads to the rehabilitation professions — the clinicians who rebuild movement after injury, illness and surgery, and the specialists who keep bodies working at every age.

roles.title: Physical Therapists
roles.what: Assess, plan, organise and participate in rehabilitative programmes that improve mobility, relieve pain and increase strength — correcting disabling conditions resulting from disease or injury across hospitals, clinics and sport.
roles.where: Unit 7's assessment and clinical reasoning is the working method; units 2 to 4 — musculoskeletal, cardiorespiratory and neurological physiotherapy — are the patient populations; unit 5's exercise prescription and return-to-sport testing is the daily craft.

roles.title: Physical Therapist Assistants
roles.what: Assist physical therapists in providing treatment — carrying out the exercises and manual techniques of the plan of care, documenting patient progress, and adjusting specific treatments within the therapist's established plan.
roles.where: Units 1 and 2 — biomechanics, exercise physiology, manual therapy — are the techniques assistants deliver under supervision; unit 7's outcome measures teach the documentation; unit 8's interprofessional working covers the therapist-assistant relationship.

roles.title: Athletic Trainers
roles.what: Evaluate and treat musculoskeletal injuries and illnesses — providing preventive, therapeutic, emergency and rehabilitative care for athletes and physically active people, on the field and in the clinic.
roles.where: Unit 2's sprains, strains and tendinopathy and unit 5's load management and return-to-sport testing are the core of the job; unit 7's special tests and their limits teaches the sideline evaluation; unit 8's ethics covers consent in sport settings.

roles.title: Exercise Physiologists
roles.what: Assess, plan and implement fitness programmes that include exercise designed to improve cardiorespiratory function, body composition, muscular strength, endurance or flexibility — often for patients recovering from or managing chronic conditions.
roles.where: Unit 1's exercise physiology is the science base; unit 3's cardiac rehabilitation and breathing exercises are classic exercise-physiologist work; unit 5's progressive overload and unit 6's special populations shape how programmes are prescribed.
